newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares fell sharply on Wednesday but losses were limited somewhat by a less steep fall than expected on Wall Street.
Dealers said the Dow Jones had been expected to sink over 100 points at the open, but the decline of the Dow Jones was halted at around minus 90 points.
The Dow Jones lingered around 70 points down as the Dutch bourse closed. "This piece of good luck is not enough to reassure the market though," said one dealer.
The AEX share index closed down nearly two percent or 11.77 points at 610.56.
Much lower bond prices and a softer dollar clouded the share market all day.
Dealers said business was likely to remain volatile for at least another week.
"All stocks in the main share index were hit today, which means it's an overall correction," said one dealer.
He said he was not able to predict a bottom for the current fall. "The market is nervous and prices will drop further: but quite how far, I have no idea," he said.
Another dealer said the AEX share index was likely to sink to 590 points within days, a level briefly hit on Friday.

The day's trading marked the second fall in a week for Dutch shares, the last time being when the AEX index crashed by over 12 points to 616.26 on Friday following the remarks made by Greenspan. The index then dropped to as low as 589.73 points, before a modest recovery.
Dealers said most Wednesday business was option-driven. Investors on the Amsterdam Option Exchange focused on the AEX-index, with some big deals in December puts.
Electronics firm Philips was down 2.40 guilders at 66.20.
Other internationals were also dragged lower in the day's hectic session. Royal Dutch shed 3.10 guilders to 283.00.
Some dealers added investors were closing their books before the end of the year and so trading was likely to be light.
"They have made very good returns this year, so it's time for them to sit back," said one.
"Good moments to start buying again are probably postponed until January," said another.
